When I was in grade school I was taught about the pre-colonial history of the Americas. I was taught about the ancient civilizations of the Inca, Aztecs, Maya and a number of the native tribes of North America. Of the Maya I was taught about their grand cities, advanced mathematics, sophisticated astronomy and observatories and their calendar and time keeping. We learned about the culture, slavery, how they differed from the Aztecs on the subject of sacrifices, but above all else we learned about the great mystery of their disappearance. I was taught that the civilization disappeared and we did not know what happened, the people were just gone. I was taught that the Maya language is a mystery that we were only just starting to make progress on being able to translate.

Many years latter I had an opportunity to work on an excavation crew in a Maya city. It was an incredibly cool opportunity and I jumped at the chance but I will admit that I was totally unqualified as a archeologist and I only got the chance because of a family member. The job consisted mostly of filling a wheelbarrow with dirt and emptying it for 10 hours a day so my lack of skill did not matter much. At the time I was working landscaping so this was about the same as what I was used to.

But I quickly realized that everything I had been taught about the Maya was total bullshit. Two days on the ground in the Yucatan and the lies I had been taught in school were laughable. In the first two days I learned the following facts while still in the city:

** THE MAYA PEOPLE DID NOT DISAPEAR** Over 40% of the current population of Yucateca (The MX providence I was in, the western half of the Yucatan peninsula) were Mayan not hispanic Mexicans. You did not need to be an expert to see this with your own eyes. Mayans do not look the same. They look a lot like the the figures in ancient art (go figure). They are short, barrel chested, and have pronounced sloping foreheads. It is impossible to ignore if you walk down the street of Merida. They Maya did not disappear... they are right fucking there.

** The MAYA CULTURE DID NOT DISAPEAR ** Want to know that the most common native language is in Yucateca? It's not Spanish... It's Maya. Thats right... for a majority of people in the region Spanish is their second language.

As I spent a month working down there I learned more. I found myself standing in the ruins of Ix'Balam (If you do a search look for "Ek' Balam" but that is not how they spell it down there). At the base of each structure there is a modern plaque with descriptions like a museum. The description on one said that we did not know what the building was for (not unusual) but we knew EXACTLY when it was built. Most of the dates on these plaques said some thing like "late classical period" or "1300 to 1450." This one said "Late 1400s to 1535" I may have the specific date wrong... it was many years ago. The point is though that the date was specific. Why? because...

** THE MAYA CIVILIZATION DID NOT DISAPPEAR ** In 1535 the city of Ix'Balam had not been abandoned. In fact it was still under construction. In 1535 Spanish Conquistadors rolled into the town to find a thriving metropolis. They promptly killed and enslaved the natives. But somehow Wikipedia claims that it was abandoned and reclaimed by the jungle only to be discovered by archeologists in the 1800s. Pack of lies.

At the end of my month I found myself in Gran Museo del Mundo Maya. This is the big official Maya museum. There is an entire room/display dedicated to The Stone Wars. I thought that by then I had learned the true history of the region but here was my last and biggest shock of all.

** THE MAYA CLAIMED INDEPENDENCE AND HAD A REBEL ARMY UNTIL 1912 ** That's right folks. In the 1500s the Spanish invaded the Maya empire and killed and raped their way from one end of the region to the other. The Maya were driven from their cities and took to the jungle. Over the next 400 years the Maya waged open war against the Spanish and the Mexican Government. Over the centuries the balance of power and who had the upper had shifted back and forth but never did the Mexican gov enjoy full control over the region. They were not able to collect taxes from the Yucatan. In the 1800s Yucateca petitioned the United States for membership in the union and statehood. It is very likely that Yucateca would have been a US state except for the fact that our own Civil War broke out and the union was in no position to adopt new states. This lasted up until 1912 when the last Maya War Chief was killed and without his leadership his army faltered. Again, if you read Wikipedia you do not get the full story. But even over there they claim the Stone Wars lasted from 1523 to 1696. 150 years of war to conquer a civilization that had already disappeared in a shroud of mystery? The lies of my early education are transparent.

Yes, there are Maya cities that were abandoned long before the Spanish got there... but it was more like what is happening today in Detroit: Every now and then people realize their town is a shit hole and everyone moves. But the great collapse of civilization we were taught about never happened.
